doc.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Bebop, band changes and the road
title: Working with Benny Carter, country players and meeting Charlie Christian
summary: Before the army he did gigs with Benny Carter, recorded with guitarists like George Van Eps, and met Charlie Christian through Lee Young.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Did you know Benny Carter while you were still in LA?
Yeah.
Did you work with him or you knew him?
Yeah, I worked with Benny, did some things with Benny.
Before you got in the army?
I might have. I might have. I worked with everybody before I got in the army, man. Hey, man, I’ve done some things with -- these country and western guitar players -- who’s the guy down there?
Alvino Ray?
No, no, man, country and western, I mean -- name some of the, you know -­
Not Bob Wills, not the Texas Playboys?
No.
You’re talking about country and western.
Stone cold country and western. Who was the head of RCA Victor, the record company down there at one time?
You got me. I mean we just saw Paul -- unless Paul has -­
Yeah. Well no, I didn’t, you know -- hey I recorded with Bonnie Castle, George Van Eps, recorded with -­
Oh, yeah, a guitarist, so you had this long association of working with the guitar.
You know, as a matter of fact I knew Charlie Christian.
Well that had to be a very short window of time.
Yeah.
So you had to meet him before you went in the army.
Oh, yeah this was before -­
Would he come through with Benny or did he come through on his own?
No, I think he was there with Benny, with Lionel, you know, Benny and Lionel. Lee Young introduced me to him. But anyway, getting back to -- where were we?
Well we were actually talking about, you know, you said you could go to Ohio and -­
Oh, yeah.
